key_insight: Coding agents can design non-neural controllers that match RL returns, but success is inconsistent and return alone does not establish robustness.
engineering_relevance: ControlHarbor tests executable controllers against explicit performance, perturbation and structural requirements, aligning agent evaluation with control-engineering practice.
method: Formulate controller design as chance-constrained feasibility.
Submit a single Python file mapping measurements to actions, without neural networks.
Evaluate on held-out seeds against ordered requirements, physical perturbations and structural certificates.
evidence_signal: Across 44 tasks over 13 plants, three frontier coding agents reached RL returns on every parity task, but only in a minority of sessions.
watch_item: Robustness remains scenario-dependent: structured design matched RL return under the humanoid robustness specification, but no designed controller succeeded under large pushes where domain-randomised RL did.
paper_title: ControlHarbor: A Benchmark for Control Design by Coding Agents
